limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.
The register below lists what the filings cannot establish and what each absence limits.

G1; Executed governing documents are not supplied: the credit agreement and its amendments, the indentures dated 2020-03-13 and 2025-09-25, and the receivables purchase agreement and amendments; no reported covenant ratio is printed in any filing; Covenant definitions, baskets, collateral, guarantor and priority terms; reported ratio for headroom; MATERIAL; Covenant headroom and legal work are not supportable; debt terms in the other modules rest on the filings' summaries; Supply the executed documents and the compliance certificate figures, or accept the filings' summaries as the only basis; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 82–85, 131; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 38

G2; No evidence dated after 2026-08-31 is supplied, 79 days before the as-of date; the third quarter of fiscal 2027 closed on 2026-10-30 by calculation; Events, financings, ratings actions or releases between 2026-09-01 and 2026-11-18; MATERIAL; Subsequent-event and liquidity statements stop at 2026-08-31; the later report is probably not yet due, by the 2025 timing; Supply any later 8-K, release or filing; until then later developments are not established; Open; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 39; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 83

G3; Discrete third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 are not supplied: the quarterly report filed 2025-12-05 is not in the folder; Four discrete quarters for trend and seasonality; MINOR; Quarterly trend is limited to the first two quarters of fiscal 2026 and of fiscal 2027; last twelve months are still computable; Supply the third-quarter report for fiscal 2026 if a quarterly series is wanted; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 83

G4; No credit rating, agency or outlook is printed or supplied; no market quotes or peers are in the run settings; Ratings, triggers, market-implied pricing, peer multiples; MINOR; Not part of the requested modules; ratings language in the filings cannot be tested; Supply rating reports and quotes if those modules are requested; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 64

G5; Letters of credit of USD 8 million are not tied to a named facility, so revolver availability net of letters of credit is not established; the revolver itself is undrawn; Undrawn revolver less letters of credit drawn on it; MINOR; Liquidity can state the USD 1.0 billion commitment but not a net availability; Obtain the credit agreement or a statement of the letter of credit sublimit; Open; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 20

G6; Cash paid for interest and for income taxes and any free cash flow figure are not printed in the quarterly reports; the 2026 annual report prints USD 101 million of cash interest and USD 22 million of cash taxes net of refunds for fiscal 2026; Cash interest and cash taxes for the interim periods and the last twelve months; MINOR; Last twelve months of cash interest cannot be built from printed figures; Request interim cash interest and tax figures or state them as not established; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 36

G7; Directors, committees, ownership and compensation are not supplied: Part III is incorporated by reference to the 2026 proxy statement; executive officers are listed; Governance and ownership detail; MINOR; Business & governance covers management and structure but not board composition or holders; Supply the proxy statement; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 76–79, 82

G8; Guarantor identities are not listed in the supplied text: wholly owned domestic subsidiaries guarantee the credit facility and the 2033 notes, the subsidiary list is an exhibit, and no guarantor financial information is printed; Guarantor perimeter and non-guarantor share of earnings and assets; MINOR; Structural priority cannot be assessed beyond the statement that domestic subsidiaries guarantee; Supply the subsidiary exhibit and the indentures; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 132, 134

G9; Presentation differences between sources, none a conflict of value: accrued payroll and vacation are regrouped in the quarterly reports (K8); the 2026 annual report moved contributions to investments out of other investing items for earlier years; cash is USD 126 million unrestricted and USD 134 million with restricted cash; the quarterly EBITDA line for interest and loss on sale of receivables (USD 35 million in the second quarter) differs from interest expense, net on the income statement (USD 33 million); One definition per line across periods and sources; MINOR; Period comparisons must use the same line definitions and the unrestricted cash figure for liquidity; Carry the regrouping and the definition differences into the financial foundation tables; Open; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 96; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 7, 31

The fiscal 2024 reported figure is flattered by the divestiture gain, and the fiscal 2026 peak reflects both lower EBITDA, down from USD 708 million to USD 676 million, and higher debt after a year in which the company borrowed USD 271 million net, paid USD 203 million for the SilverEdge acquisition and returned USD 515 million to shareholders. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Definitions flatter leverage and cover. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Cash interest paid for the first half of fiscal 2026 and 2027 is not printed in the quarterly reports, so last-twelve-months EBITDA over cash interest cannot be calculated; it restricts interest cover to fiscal years, and the action that closes it is the interim cash flow supplement or an issuer statement of cash interest. Severity: High. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 36 - The reported ratio and the definitions for the Senior Secured Leverage Ratio of at most 4.00 to 1.00 are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the accounting leverage in this module cannot be compared with the covenant; the action is the credit agreement and the compliance figure. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 131, 133 - No filing states the security, guarantee or ranking of the senior notes due April 2028 (principal 400), so they are left out of the debt stack and of the senior unsecured line, and the stack is a partial one; the action is the indenture. Severity: Medium. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14 - Letters of credit of 8 are not tied to a facility, so revolver availability net of letters of credit is not established and the undrawn figures are gross; the action is the credit agreement letter of credit terms. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 20 - The revolver commitment and balance at 2024-02-02 are not stated for that date, so fiscal 2024 undrawn capacity and the fiscal 2024 liquidity ratio are not supplied; the action is the fiscal 2024 annual report note. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-01-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 134, 135 - The third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 are not supplied as discrete quarters because the third-quarter report is not in the folder, so no quarterly series beyond the first two quarters of each year is built; the last twelve months are still computable. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 83 - Dashes printed in the statements are carried as not supplied rather than zero, in particular the divestiture gain for fiscal 2025 and 2026, other operating income in the first half of fiscal 2026 and second quarter of fiscal 2027, acquisition cash in all periods but fiscal 2026, debt issuance costs in fiscal 2024 and 2025 and borrowing proceeds in the first half of fiscal 2027; none of them changes a ratio, and the action is a statement from the issuer that each dash means nil. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4 - Lines the quarterly reports do not present are marked not supplied for those columns, including the divestiture gain, the sale of equity method investments, proceeds from divestitures, debt issuance costs, stock-based compensation for the second quarter alone, and cash taxes paid; the action is to read the annual report for year-level figures. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4 - Funds from operations is not defined by the issuer and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, so funds from operations ratios are not calculable and total capital expenditure is used; the action is an issuer definition. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93 - Net bookings are rounded estimates, and fiscal 2024 bookings and the fiscal 2024 sold receivables balance are not extracted; they affect operating indicators only. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 136 - The balance sheet at 2025-08-01 is not supplied because the second-quarter report for fiscal 2026 is not in the folder, so the first half of fiscal 2026 column has income and cash flow but no balance sheet. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 3 - The defined benefit pension and retiree plan funded positions are small and sit inside other assets and other liabilities; they are not extracted as separate lines and do not enter Total Debt. Severity: Low. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 127

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Customer concentration is very high but cushioned by contract type. Federal customers supply 98% of revenue and cost-reimbursement contracts supply 61.76% against 15.75% for firm-fixed-price work, so most cost increases are passed through to the customer while volume depends on appropriations: the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and open audits by the government's cost auditor can still disallow billed costs. The mechanism that matters for creditors is lost or delayed volume, not margin. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 142; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 23; calculation A06

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder returns have priority over deleveraging. Buybacks and dividends of USD 515 million took 89.25% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million and, with the USD 203 million SilverEdge acquisition, exceeded it by USD 141 million; in the first half of fiscal 2027 returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow of USD 249 million. The dividend of USD 0.37 per share each quarter is small beside the buyback, which the board authorised up to USD 1,200 million in December 2024, so returns can be cut quickly, but the filings do not commit the board to do so and say only that dividends and buybacks may be limited at certain leverage ratios. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 64, 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04

facts.text: The filings state no sponsor, buyout, recapitalisation or pending acquisition financing. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: SAIC is listed on Nasdaq with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named, so creditors have no sponsor to inject equity and no sponsor to extract it. The credit facility is secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by each wholly owned domestic subsidiary, and the notes due November 2033 are unsecured and guaranteed by the same subsidiaries. Financial policy is set by the board: dividends and buybacks may be limited at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium because returns absorb most free cash flow and an antitrust investigation is open. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is driven by volume on existing contracts and new awards, with little price lever: contracts generally provide labour on a reimbursable basis and cost-type contracts pass costs through. Revenue is concentrated, regulated and budget-cyclical rather than economically cyclical, and renewal of task orders each year refreshes bookings. ## Request

Source readiness for Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the registrant's four supplied SEC filings, assessed for the Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work; no earlier run of this pathway exists.
## Sources

No upstream handoff was supplied to this module; it is the first module of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The four SAIC filings support the requested financial foundation, business profile and fundamental credit work as of the quarter ended July 31, 2026, but not covenant headroom, ratings or events after August 31, 2026. Creditors should therefore treat any conclusion on those three points as outside the evidence.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 14, 39; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 82–85, 131

Every debt instrument, the undrawn revolving facility, the receivables sale facility, leases, retirement plans and contingent items are described in the notes, so debt and claims outside debt can be built from the filings alone. The credit agreement, the indentures and the receivables agreement are named in the exhibit lists but not supplied, and the covenant ratio appears only as a compliance statement. The newest filing was signed 79 days before the as-of date.

spans.text: # Financial foundation: Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123)
## Request

Financial foundation for Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the consolidated registrant's statements, debt, liquidity and credit ratios from fiscal 2024 to the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with the last twelve months built from the 2026 annual report and the fiscal 2027 quarterly reports.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 1, 2026 | 2026-06-01 (signature date) | 15b02455195764742ac1639f71f7b679b44800457579f88b76afb03edf6336f3 | Debt table and covenant statement at 2026-05-01; first-quarter figures tied to the six-month figures of the later report (calculation C32) |

## Findings
### Bottom line

SAIC's reported leverage is 3.29x gross and 3.12x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA at July 31, 2026, and fiscal 2026 cash interest cover was 6.69x; these are accounting ratios, not the covenant test, whose headroom cannot be established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 131; calculation C10

Gross leverage rose from 2.36x in fiscal 2024 mainly because that year's reported EBITDA included a USD 240 million divestiture gain; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA it was 3.14x then and is 3.18x now. Net debt rose by USD 54 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 because shareholder returns of USD 319 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 249 million.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 31; calculation C09; calculation C20; calculation C21
### Key findings

Leverage has moved less than the reported series suggests. Gross debt over reported EBITDA was 2.36x at fiscal 2024, 3.14x at fiscal 2025, 3.68x at fiscal 2026 and 3.29x on the last twelve months to July 31, 2026, while gross debt over issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 3.14x, 3.13x, 3.51x and 3.18x. The fiscal 2024 reported figure is flattered by the divestiture gain, and the fiscal 2026 peak reflects both lower EBITDA, down from USD 708 million to USD 676 million, and higher debt after a year in which the company borrowed USD 271 million net, paid USD 203 million for the SilverEdge acquisition and returned USD 515 million to shareholders.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 93, 131; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14; calculation C10; calculation C19; calculation C20

Cash generation is strong but leans on items that can reverse. Operating cash flow was USD 609 million in fiscal 2026 and free cash flow USD 577 million, or 85.36% of reported EBITDA, yet cash taxes paid were USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, and collections of receivables added USD 161 million. Sales of receivables sit inside operating cash flow, so a smaller facility balance lowers it, as when the facility cut operating cash flow by USD 41 million in fiscal 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129, 136; calculation C09; calculation C27

Shareholder returns, not operations, are what lift net debt. In fiscal 2026 buybacks and dividends of USD 515 million and the USD 203 million acquisition exceeded free cash flow, and net debt rose by USD 141 million; in the first half of fiscal 2027 returns of USD 319 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 249 million, taking net debt to USD 2,359 million.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4; calculation C02; calculation C20; calculation C21

Near-term liquidity and maturities are not pressing. Unrestricted cash is USD 126 million and the USD 1,000 million revolver due September 2030 is undrawn, so committed resources are USD 1,126 million before USD 8 million of letters of credit whose facility the filings do not name; scheduled maturities are USD 48 million through fiscal 2028 and USD 489 million in fiscal 2029, mostly the notes due April 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14, 15, 20; calculation C18; calculation C25

Definitions flatter leverage and cover. EBITDA adds back interest and the loss on sold receivables of USD 140 million in fiscal 2026 against interest expense of USD 128 million, so USD 12 million of receivables financing cost is left out of EBITDA, and USD 120 million of sold receivables at July 31, 2026 stay outside debt. Cash interest of USD 101 million is below the USD 128 million expense, which lifts cash cover.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 91, 93, 136; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C28; calculation C30
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that last-twelve-months gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x of fiscal 2026, that the USD 1,000 million revolver is undrawn and that maturities are small until fiscal 2029. It would win if first-half reported EBITDA growth of 24.02% persists and free cash flow again covers shareholder returns.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 31; calculation C10; calculation C26

The evidence for concern is that net debt has risen in every period since fiscal 2024, that revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 and that 98% of revenue comes from one customer, the U.S. government. A fall in federal funding, or an adverse result in the Department of Justice investigation, which the company says it cannot estimate, would change the view.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 140; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C02; calculation C26
### Limitations
Cash interest is not printed for interim periods, so cash interest cover cannot be updated beyond fiscal 2026 and last-twelve-months cover is not calculable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 36
The covenant ratio is not reported and the debt documents are not supplied, so none of these ratios is a covenant measure and headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 131
The senior notes due April 2028 carry no stated security or rank, so they are left out of the debt stack and its cumulative figures are partial.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 134

Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4

- Funds from operations is not defined by the issuer and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, so funds from operations ratios are not calculable and total capital expenditure is used; the action is an issuer definition. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93
- Net bookings are rounded estimates, and fiscal 2024 bookings and the fiscal 2024 sold receivables balance are not extracted; they affect operating indicators only. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 136

- The balance sheet at 2025-08-01 is not supplied because the second-quarter report for fiscal 2026 is not in the folder, so the first half of fiscal 2026 column has income and cash flow but no balance sheet. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The defined benefit pension and retiree plan funded positions are small and sit inside other assets and other liabilities; they are not extracted as separate lines and do not enter Total Debt. Severity: Low.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123)
## Request

Business, ownership and governance review of Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the registrant's business, ownership, operating model, issuer history, governance and capital-allocation behaviour, from its four filings to the quarter ended 2026-07-31; no earlier run of this pathway exists.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-01-31_saic.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 | 2025-03-17 (signature date; the 2026 annual report exhibit list gives the same day as the filing date) | aed24f8560478e402aa66163efd359b8828e79388953966a434b03c0277de317 | Refinancing and divestiture history of fiscal 2024 and 2025; credit agreement amendments of 2024 |

| 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 30, 2026 | 2026-03-16 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 25b6d045feac13f51bbd4a2b45e12c4a384a9fe75310b9b40aca4dd1d1e71329 | Primary evidence for business, customers, contract mix, competition, officers, legal matters, shareholder returns, debt events and the exhibit list |

| 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 1, 2026 | 2026-06-01 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 15b02455195764742ac1639f71f7b679b44800457579f88b76afb03edf6336f3 | Read for continuity of the first quarter of fiscal 2027; no figure in this module rests on it alone |

| 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 | 2026-08-31 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 14b4f4b255cf2da0c5fb957a45e6f958cfdee3ddd794b4e4542a5aac7a553406 | Latest backlog, segment mix, cash flows, legal matters, share count and subsequent events |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 4f114a892bdecc310206a6f96ea9678c18c99f9a2b84e0104a8d28eb0a0c837a | Inventory of the four filings and the list of documents not supplied: governing legal documents, proxy statement, ratings and anything after 2026-08-31 |
## Findings
### Bottom line

SAIC is a listed, mostly cost-reimbursed U.S. government contractor with no sponsor identified, so creditors depend on contract cash flows and board restraint rather than outside support, and shareholder returns took 89.25% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 79, 82, 93; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03

Revenue is almost wholly federal, 98% in fiscal 2026 and 52.02% from the Department of War, and USD 22,136 million of backlog at July 31, 2026 gives visibility, but only USD 3,818 million of it is funded. A criminal antitrust investigation is open with no estimate of penalties, the chief executive changed in October 2025, and a funding lapse or contract review would hit volume directly.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 77, 140; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 34; calculation A05
### Key findings

No sponsor stands behind the debt, and none is drawing value out of it. The filings name no parent, sponsor or controlling holder; the shares are listed on Nasdaq and held by about seventeen thousand holders of record, so there is no sponsor support to count on and no sponsor-led recapitalisation to fear. Holdings of large stockholders sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so concentration among them is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 79, 82; Source readiness (CP-0)

Customer concentration is very high but cushioned by contract type. Federal customers supply 98% of revenue and cost-reimbursement contracts supply 61.76% against 15.75% for firm-fixed-price work, so most cost increases are passed through to the customer while volume depends on appropriations: the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and open audits by the government's cost auditor can still disallow billed costs. The mechanism that matters for creditors is lost or delayed volume, not margin.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 142; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 23; calculation A06

Backlog gives visibility, but little of it is funded and it is not growing. Total backlog was USD 22,136 million at July 31, 2026 against USD 22,622 million at January 30, 2026, only USD 3,818 million of it, or 17.25%, is funded, and net bookings of about USD 3.3 billion in the half were 0.87 times revenue. Remaining performance obligations are USD 6.4 billion, of which 75% is expected within twelve months, so most of the backlog still needs later funding or the exercise of options before it becomes revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 34; calculation A09; calculation A10; calculation A13

Shareholder returns have priority over deleveraging. Buybacks and dividends of USD 515 million took 89.25% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million and, with the USD 203 million SilverEdge acquisition, exceeded it by USD 141 million; in the first half of fiscal 2027 returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow of USD 249 million. The dividend of USD 0.37 per share each quarter is small beside the buyback, which the board authorised up to USD 1,200 million in December 2024, so returns can be cut quickly, but the filings do not commit the board to do so and say only that dividends and buybacks may be limited at certain leverage ratios.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 47, 64, 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04

Leadership and structure changed together, which raises execution risk in a period when revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 and grew 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027. The chief executive and other executives left in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, an interim chief executive served from October 2025 until February 2026, executive transition costs of USD 16 million net were added back in adjusted EBITDA, and five business groups were consolidated into three from 2026-01-31 with both reportable segments unchanged.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 58, 60, 77; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation A14

An open criminal antitrust investigation is the main unquantified claim. The company received federal grand jury subpoenas in April 2022 and October 2023, is producing documents and says it cannot estimate fines or penalties; separately it warns that adverse findings in government investigations and audits can lead to suspension or debarment, which for a business with 98% federal revenue would threaten most of its revenue if it occurred.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 140, 142; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 19
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more benign view is that several customer relationships have lasted 20 years or more, that 61.76% of revenue is cost-reimbursed, that backlog is 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, and that returns to shareholders are discretionary, so the board could retain cash quickly. The view would move toward benign if returns fell back below free cash flow for several quarters and the investigation closed without a penalty.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 115; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation A06; calculation A12

It would move toward cautious if revenue fell again after the 2.90% decline of fiscal 2026, if returns again exceeded free cash flow while net debt rose, or if a penalty, a debarment proceeding or a funding lapse longer than the 2026 shutdown appeared. The first-half revenue growth of 3.84% is partly acquired, since SilverEdge added USD 39 million, and the company puts growth excluding acquisitions at about 2.9%, so it does not by itself show recovery.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation A14
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, stockholder concentration and related-party dealings are not established; this weakens the conclusion that no controlling holder exists, which rests on the holder count and the absence of any named sponsor.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 82; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The leverage level at which dividends and buybacks would be limited is not printed and the credit agreement is not supplied, so how far returns could rise before the credit facility stops them is not established; the shareholder-return finding rests on conduct alone.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 64; Source readiness (CP-0)
- The investigation has no disclosed estimate or timetable, so the contingent-claim finding is open-ended and could move the view in either direction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 19

- The filings end on 2026-08-31, before the federal fiscal year that began on 2026-10-01, so whether appropriations lapsed again or the backlog moved since then is not established; this limits the funding-risk finding to the position at the end of August.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 34
- Results are disclosed only for the two reportable segments, so the effect of the consolidation into three business groups on any one group is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 16

## Findings
### Bottom line

SAIC is an adequate credit: cost-reimbursed federal contracts and light capital needs give free cash flow, but shareholder returns that absorb most of it, a mostly unfunded backlog and one dominant customer cap it, leaving gross leverage at 3.29x and net debt rising.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 115; calculation F01; calculation F04; calculation F05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Shareholder returns, not operations, set the leverage path, and the first-half earnings surge is fading, with second-quarter adjusted EBITDA up only 4.32%. The main downside is a federal funding or contract-review shock that cuts volume while returns keep lifting net debt; no covenant ratio is reported, so headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24, 31; calculation F06; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

Cash flow is durable because most revenue is cost-reimbursed and capital needs are light. Cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million was 85.36% of reported EBITDA and last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt. Fiscal 2026 cash flow was helped by receivables collections of USD 161 million and cash taxes of USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, so it should not be extrapolated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 93, 129; calculation F05; calculation F04; calculation F18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Revenue visibility is thinner than the backlog suggests. Backlog is USD 22,136 million, or 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, but only 17.25% is funded, net bookings were 0.87 times revenue in the first half after 1.07 times in fiscal 2026, and revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 before growing 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027, of which about 2.9% was organic. Funding lapses and contract reviews are the channel through which unfunded backlog turns into lost or delayed revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24, 27, 34; calculation F05; calculation F10; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings momentum is real but slowing, which corrects the weight Financial foundation puts on first-half growth. Reported EBITDA rose 24.02% in the first half, but the gain was front-loaded: it rose 41.03% in the first quarter and 9.04% in the second, when adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% and its margin slipped to 10.3% from 10.5% despite organic revenue growth of about 5.3%. The first half also includes a USD 12 million gain on the sale of an investment that the adjusted measure does not remove; without it adjusted EBITDA growth is 17.84%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 27, 31; calculation F02; calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F09; calculation F08; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is moderate on the issuer's own definitions but is set by shareholder returns. Gross debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA is 3.29x, 3.18x on adjusted EBITDA and 3.12x net, or 3.14x net pro forma for the USD 15.5 million dividend payable on 2026-10-23; net debt is USD 2,359 million, or USD 2,374.5 million pro forma. Returns of USD 515 million took 89.25% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and, with the USD 203 million acquisition, exceeded it, and returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow in the first half of fiscal 2027, lifting net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million; each further USD 100 million of net debt adds 0.13x. This corrects the operating map in Business & governance, which says returns exceeded free cash flow in both periods: on their own they did so only in the first half of fiscal 2027.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable until the notes due April 2028. Liquidity is USD 1,126 million, mostly the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver, before the dividend payable on 2026-10-23 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, and it covers the USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 23.46 times; USD 489 million falls due in fiscal 2029, mostly the USD 400 million notes. Term loan amortisation rises from USD 27.50 million to USD 82.50 million a year from late 2028, and 63.99% of principal floats after the interest rate swaps expired, so 50 bp costs about USD 8 million a year.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 132, 135; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F03; calculation F16; calculation F13; calculation F14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Event risk sits in the antitrust investigation, federal funding and contract reviews. The company cannot estimate fines or penalties in the investigation, the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and agencies are reviewing contracts, although the company reports no material financial effect so far. Governance does not offset these risks: there is no sponsor, the credit agreement may limit dividends and buybacks only at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 23, 24; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation F05; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that adjusted leverage has stayed between 3.13x and 3.51x over four periods, that last-twelve-months gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x of fiscal 2026, that the revolver is undrawn and that returns are discretionary. A board that kept returns below free cash flow for several quarters, with the investigation closed without a penalty, would justify a stronger view.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F01; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A weaker view would follow if adjusted EBITDA growth stayed near the 4.32% of the second quarter, if net bookings stayed below revenue, if a funding lapse lasted longer than the 2026 shutdown, or if the investigation ended in a penalty or a debarment proceeding. Falling back to the fiscal 2026 EBITDA level would put gross leverage at 3.68x, and that is the level the company has already lived with, so the view turns on earnings momentum and the board's payout choices, not on liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation F06; calculation F10; calculation F15; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Limitations
- No peer, sector or market data is supplied, so the adequate label rests on the issuer's own history and the filings, not on comparison with other credits, and the sector discussion is qualitative.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- The filings contain no guidance or projections, so the outlook and the downside case rest on reported trends and the company's own risk statements and carry no forecast.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Evidence ends on 2026-08-31, so whether the second-quarter margin dip became a trend, and what followed the start of the federal year on 2026-10-01, is not established; this limits the earnings-momentum finding to the first half.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 31

- Free cash flow as computed from the filings is helped by receivables collections and low cash taxes, and no normalised figure is supplied, so cash conversion is stated as reported and may overstate the repeatable level.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Company description

SAIC sells technical, engineering and IT services almost entirely to the U.S. government: 98% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 97% in the first half of fiscal 2027, with the Department of War alone at 52.02%. Customer relationships include several of 20 years or more, and cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue, so cash flow is visible and cost-protected, but it depends on annual appropriations and on contracts that customers may end for convenience, recovering only the costs incurred and profit on work done.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 9, 10; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation F05; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The credit link is direct: stable, cost-protected cash flow supports debt service and refinancing confidence, while concentration in one buyer means a funding lapse reaches revenue at once, as the shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security from February to April 2026 showed. A government shutdown also cut fiscal 2026 revenue by about USD 26 million.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

SAIC is listed on Nasdaq with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named, so creditors have no sponsor to inject equity and no sponsor to extract it. The credit facility is secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by each wholly owned domestic subsidiary, and the notes due November 2033 are unsecured and guaranteed by the same subsidiaries. Financial policy is set by the board: dividends and buybacks may be limited at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium because returns absorb most free cash flow and an antitrust investigation is open.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 64, 132, 134; calculation F05; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is driven by volume on existing contracts and new awards, with little price lever: contracts generally provide labour on a reimbursable basis and cost-type contracts pass costs through. Revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 on contract completions and ramp-downs, including the shutdown effect, and was about 3.3% lower excluding SilverEdge; it grew 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027, of which about 2.9% was organic and 5.3% in the second quarter alone. Revenue is concentrated, regulated and budget-cyclical rather than economically cyclical, and renewal of task orders each year refreshes bookings.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; calculation F05; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Visibility is partial. Backlog of USD 22,136 million is 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, but only 17.25% is funded, net bookings were 0.88 times revenue in fiscal 2025, 1.07 times in fiscal 2026 and 0.87 times in the first half, and the company says greater use of competitive multi-award contracts and small-business set-asides has raised pricing pressure and reduced the addressable market. The implication is that revenue growth must come from winning work, not from pricing.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 34; calculation F05; calculation F10; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are mostly labour and pass-through: in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 the labour base was 28.19% of revenue, other operating expenses, mainly subcontractors and materials, 61.65%, and adjusted operating income 10.16%, while in fiscal 2026 cost of revenues was 87.99% of revenue and operating income 7.17%. With cost-reimbursement contracts at 61.76% of revenue, inflation risk is limited, and the company says inflation has not had a significant effect in three years; the margin risk sits in the 15.75% of fixed-price work and in contract mix.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 91; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation F05; calculation F11; calculation F12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margins are improving but the pace is slowing. Last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA margin is 10.55%, the first quarter was 11.6% against 8.4% a year earlier, and the second quarter slipped to 10.3% from 10.5% despite organic revenue growth of about 5.3%. Operating leverage is low because costs follow volume, so margins can be defended under volume pressure on cost-type work, but a mix shift toward fixed price or a decline in volume would lower them first.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 31; calculation F09; calculation F07
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is minimal: capital expenditure was 0.44% of revenue in fiscal 2026, so there is little capital flexibility to find but also little need. Free cash flow of USD 577 million was 85.36% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and USD 619 million over the last twelve months, equal to 24.91% of gross debt, which is sizeable relative to debt on these definitions.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation F05; calculation F04; calculation F18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Conversion is helped by items that can reverse: receivables collections of USD 161 million in fiscal 2026 and cash taxes of USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, while receivables absorbed cash in the first half of fiscal 2027. Sales of receivables sit inside operating cash flow, so the facility, raised to USD 400 million after the quarter end, can move cash between periods without changing debt. The durable level of free cash flow is therefore below the reported peak and is not quantified in the filings.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20; calculation F04; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Porter's Five Forces

Competitive rivalry is intense and raises pricing pressure. Large defense primes, technical services peers and diversified commercial providers all compete, sole-source awards are fewer, and multi-award vehicles increase competition, which caps margins on re-competes and makes bookings the key indicator.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 24

The threat of new entrants is moderate. Security clearances held by most of the workforce and past performance protect incumbents, but other-transaction agreements lower barriers to entry and small-business set-asides reduce the addressable market, so share loss is a gradual, not sudden, risk.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 24

Buyer power is very high. One buyer provides 97% to 98% of revenue, it may terminate contracts for convenience and it funds work by annual appropriation, so any adverse change in budgets or contract priorities reaches volume directly; cost recovery on terminated work softens the loss.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10, 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23

Supplier power is moderate and sits in labour. Cleared talent is scarce and competitors recruit aggressively, and subcontractors can fail to perform, but cost-type contracts pass wage and subcontract costs through, so the exposure is mainly on fixed-price work.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 34, 72
The filings describe no substitute for outsourced government services; the substitution-like risk is the government reducing or reviewing contracts, which is covered under buyer power.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are the primary credit driver: appropriations, shutdowns, continuing resolutions, executive orders and agency contract reviews set volume, and the company's own statement is that it has not seen a material financial effect from recent orders or cancellations. Economic factors are secondary but real on the liability side: 63.99% of principal floats, so rates matter more than inflation, which cost-type contracts largely absorb. Social and technological factors are not primary drivers; demand for digital modernization, cyber and AI services is an opportunity rather than a risk to repayment.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 135; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24; calculation F13
### SWOT analysis

Strengths are federal revenue with cost-type protection, light capital needs, free cash flow of 24.91% of gross debt, a USD 1,000 million undrawn revolver and maturities of only USD 48 million through fiscal 2028. Weaknesses are one dominant customer, a backlog that is mostly unfunded, net debt rising with returns that absorb free cash flow, and no reported covenant ratio.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F18; calculation F03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The opportunities that could improve credit quality are demand for digital modernization, cyber and AI services and organic growth of about 5.3% in the second quarter, which would help deleveraging only if returns were held below free cash flow. Threats are a funding lapse, contract reviews and set-asides that reduce volume, the open antitrust investigation, and the refinancing of USD 400 million of notes due April 2028 at a time when gross leverage is 3.29x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 24, 27; calculation F07; calculation F01; calculation F03; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is cash-flow durability: cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so most cost increases are passed through and free cash flow of USD 577 million covered debt service in fiscal 2026. The second is liquidity and maturity shape: USD 1,126 million of liquidity against USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 means no refinancing is needed before the notes due April 2028. The third is customer longevity: several relationships of 20 years or more and a USD 22,136 million backlog support renewal of work.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 93, 115; calculation F05; calculation F03; calculation F16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow, 89.25% in fiscal 2026 and 128.11% in the first half of fiscal 2027, which with the acquisition lifted net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million with no sponsor or covenant ratio to restrain them. The second is dependence on one buyer, with 52.02% of revenue from the Department of War and 17.25% of backlog funded, so a funding or contract-review shock cuts volume. The third is fading momentum: second-quarter adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% against 24.02% reported for the half, and net bookings were 0.87 times revenue. The fourth is an unquantified antitrust investigation and floating-rate exposure of 63.99% of principal.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 31, 34; calculation F04; calculation F05; calculation F06; calculation F10; calculation F13; calculation F02; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are scale, cost-type revenue and cash generation. Scale is a strength: revenue of USD 7,402 million over the last twelve months is a large base for a services contractor, and free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because costs follow volume and capital needs are 0.44% of revenue, and margin stability is average, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.55% but a slip to 10.3% in the second quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation F02; calculation F18; calculation F05; calculation F09; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The constraints are concentration, financial policy and visibility. Business diversification is weak, because one buyer provides 97% to 98% of revenue and the Department of War 52.02%; competitive advantage is average, resting on 20-year relationships and clearances against rising price pressure. Free cash flow stability is average, since conversion of 85.36% in fiscal 2026 leans on receivables collections and low cash taxes. Financial policy and governance is average: reporting and audit quality are sound and returns are discretionary, but returns of 89.25% and 128.11% of free cash flow are not restrained by a sponsor or a printed covenant ratio, which is why governance risk is Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation F05; calculation F04; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Ability to refinance and access markets is average: the revolver and term loan A run to September 2030 and USD 400 million of notes fall due in April 2028, but no rating or market quote is supplied, so access is judged from the maturity profile alone. Liquidity is a strength at USD 1,126 million, before the dividend payable on 2026-10-23 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established. The trend is stable on adjusted leverage and rising on net debt, which was USD 2,359 million, or USD 2,374.5 million pro forma for that dividend; the missing datapoints are the covenant ratio, interim cash interest, any rating and evidence after 2026-08-31.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F03; calculation F01; Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is stable with a bias to slower earnings growth. Tailwinds are USD 6.4 billion of remaining performance obligations, 75% of which the company expects to recognise within twelve months, organic growth of about 5.3% in the second quarter and low capital needs. Headwinds are net bookings of 0.87 times revenue, a margin that slipped in the second quarter, a rise in term loan A amortisation from USD 27.50 million to USD 55.00 million a year from 2027-10-31, and a federal year that started after the filings end.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27, 31; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 132; calculation F07; calculation F10; calculation F14; calculation F09

Over three to five years the outlook turns on refinancing and payout choices rather than on operations. Maturities are USD 48 million through fiscal 2028, then USD 489 million in fiscal 2029, USD 88 million in fiscal 2030 and USD 899 million in fiscal 2031, so the notes due April 2028 and the term loan A balloon are the tests; gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x at which the company ended fiscal 2026, after refinancing in September 2025, but each USD 100 million of returns funded by debt adds 0.13x. Sector tailwinds are spending packages for digital modernization and cyber; sector headwinds are shutdowns, continuing resolutions, contract reviews and set-asides, and the company says it is well positioned, which is management language and not evidence.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 24; calculation F03; calculation F01; calculation F17; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside is a funding lapse or an agency contract review that cuts volume while shareholder returns continue. The first operational break would be delayed or stopped work on civilian and defense programs, as in the shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security from February to April 2026 and the shutdown that cut fiscal 2026 revenue by about USD 26 million; backlog is 17.25% funded, so most future work depends on later funding. Revenue and EBITDA would fall, but with 61.76% of revenue cost-reimbursed the margin falls less than volume, and the exposure is concentrated in the 15.75% of fixed-price work.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24; calculation F05; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial transmission is arithmetic. If last-twelve-months EBITDA returned to the fiscal 2026 level of USD 676 million, a fall of 10.58%, gross leverage would be 3.68x, the same as at the end of fiscal 2026, and if returns continued at the first-half level of USD 319 million while free cash flow fell, net debt would rise faster, with each USD 100 million adding 0.13x. Liquidity of USD 1,126 million is 23.46 times maturities through fiscal 2028, so liquidity distress is not in prospect; the lever is the board's choice to cut buybacks, which were USD 445 million in fiscal 2026, and the dividend, which was USD 70 million. A refinancing of the April 2028 notes at leverage of 3.68x is the first financing consequence; the covenant effect is not established because the ratio is not reported. An adverse result in the antitrust investigation, including debarment, would be a separate and larger break and is not sized.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation F15; calculation F17; calculation F16; calculation F04; calculation F03; calculation F01; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Overall credit view

Overall, SAIC presents an adequate business profile supported by cost-reimbursed federal revenue, light capital needs and a seasoned customer base, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on one buyer, a mostly unfunded backlog, and shareholder returns that absorb most free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt, although conversion is flattered by receivables collections and low cash taxes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings momentum, which slowed in the second quarter, and on whether the board keeps returns below free cash flow before the notes due April 2028.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation F18; calculation F06; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The primary downside path is a funding lapse or contract review that cuts volume while returns continue to lift net debt. The profile is not benchmarked against typical leveraged-credit issuers because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant ratio, the proxy statement, interim cash interest, any rating, and evidence after 2026-08-31. Fundamental credit is complete. Top risk: shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow while one customer funds the business.
